candidate.title: TRIBE
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina schematic of original Drosophila ADAR catalytic-domain TRIBE (Targets of RNA-binding proteins Identified By Editing): fusion design, cell-specific expression and RNA association, A-to-I target marking, and a cDNA G-signature endpoint. The leftmost target-identification icon states the aim; the native ADAR domain drawing explains fusion design. Neither is another workflow. The catalogue downstream library interface clarifies how the depicted cDNA is read, without expanding the graph into unshown cell isolation, amplification, or library-preparation steps.

operations.label: Create TRIBE fusion protein
operations.description: Engineer an RBP-ADARcd fusion by joining the RBP and Drosophila ADAR catalytic-domain coding sequences. The drawn protein-domain combination is represented here by its expression construct, as supported by the primary cloning description. Native ADAR is an explanatory domain reference, not a separate assay branch or a mature protein cut apart in this operation.
operations.mechanism: Genetic fusion replaces native ADAR RNA-recognition domains with the RBP of interest while retaining the ADAR catalytic component.
operations.information_effect: Couples the identity and RNA-recognition properties of the chosen RBP to a local RNA-editing reporter.

operations.label: Cell-specific expression of fusion protein
operations.description: Use the fusion-encoding construct as an expression template in the cells of interest. The expressed fusion binds an RNA target through its RBP domain, producing the fusion-associated, still A-containing RNA shown in this panel. The construct is a template input, and the cellular RNA is the eventual editing substrate.
operations.mechanism: Cell-specific expression produces the RBP-ADARcd protein; RBP-mediated recognition brings its catalytic domain to the target RNA.
operations.information_effect: Restricts the origin of fusion-induced marks to cells expressing this fusion and associates an RBP recognition event with an RNA molecule.

operations.label: Binding site marked by I
operations.description: The RNA-bound fusion catalyzes conversion of a proximal adenosine to inosine. The output differs from the input RNA by a persistent base modification; no RNA-fragment capture or cleavage step is depicted.
operations.mechanism: The ADAR catalytic domain deaminates RNA adenosine to inosine; the fusion is the catalyst, rather than a component covalently incorporated into the RNA.
operations.information_effect: The edited RNA permanently records an interaction with the fusion. This supports identification of target transcripts and approximate binding regions, not exact binding nucleotides. Editable adenosine availability and ADARcd structural/sequence preferences limit which bound targets can be marked; an unedited RNA is not proof of absent binding.

operations.label: cDNA. Binding site marked by G
operations.description: Convert the edited RNA into cDNA, resolving the final arrow as reverse transcription using the catalogue description. The I-containing RNA gives rise to the G-equivalent sequence signature drawn in the RNA-sense cDNA/readout representation. The figure leaves library generation broad and unshown beyond this cDNA endpoint.
operations.mechanism: Inosine is recognized as guanosine during copying/readout. The G cartoon does not specify that the immediate first-strand cDNA contains G at that position.
operations.information_effect: Retains the target transcript sequence and converts the persistent RNA edit into an A-to-G signature recoverable by sequencing a derived cDNA library. Novel fusion-associated edits identify target transcripts after accounting for genomic variation and endogenous editing; they do not establish exhaustive binding specificity.

method_scopes.rationale: All four local operations apply to the single TRIBE workflow named by the card and the matching collection heading/caption. The primary paper establishes the RBP-Drosophila ADARcd implementation underlying the schematic. The native ADAR A-to-I icon is a component/activity explanation, not a parallel endogenous-editing assay. TruSeq is a downstream library-preparation component named in the catalogue, and the paper's CLIP comparisons and individual RBP applications do not create additional target methods.
